Ubinadamu umefafanuliwa kwa kutafuta kweli. Watu wengine hutafuta ukweli huu kupitia nguvu zao binafsi, wakijaribu kuwatawala wenzao. Wengine hutafuta ukweli katika furaha, wakiona kuridhika binafsi kama mafanikio makuu maishani. Wengine wanatafuta mwanga kupitia mawazo na mantiki zao wenyewe, wakizidi kujifunza, wala kamwe wasiwezi kufika kwenye maarifa ya ukweli – 2 Timotheo 3:7. Wengine zaidi wanaamini maisha ya utumishi yatakuwa zawadi yenyewe, kwa hivyo wanajaribu kujipatia jina kupitia uenezaji wa matendo yao ya huduma na wema.

Mara kwa mara, katika historia, fikra za kikundi la watu zimegeukia kitu kikubwa zaidi ya wao wenyewe. Dini zinainuka, na dini zinapungua, milki zinaanzishwa na kuanguka, tamaduni za fikra zinajengwa na kuvunjika.

Kinyume na mzunguko huu wa mawazo, harakati ambayo wasomaji wengi wangu watatambua, ilianza katika eneo dogo lenye milima duniani. Zurich, Uswisi, mwaka wa 1525 BK, ilikuwa itakuwa mahali na tarehe yake ya kuzaliwa, lakini mizizi yake ilianzishwa miaka elfu moja na mia tano kabla yake, katika Galilaya, pale Ambaye alipofundisha na kuishi majibu ya mwisho kwa maswali yote ya mwanadamu.

Mwanzo wa harakati hizi za hivi karibuni umeandikwa vyema. Kwa kifupi, ilianzishwa na kikundi kidogo cha wanafunzi mbalimbali, wahubiri, na watu wa kawaida waliotafuta ukweli katika umbo lake safi. Hadithi za Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz, na George Blaurock zinajulikana kwa wengi wetu. Walijitahidi kutenga kutoka kwa uharibifu wa kiroho uliowazunguka, walipoanzisha mwanzo wa kile kilichoitwa harakati ya Anabaptist.

Hawa watatu walikabili ukaguzi wa mamlaka za kiraia na kiroho za wakati wao, wakivumilia mateso na maumivu kwa ajili ya imani yao. Wawili miongoni mwao hatimaye walitoa maisha yao kwa ajili ya ukweli waliouheshimu sana. Felix Manz alikuwa Anabaptist wa kwanza kuuawa kifo kwa imani. Mnamo Januari 5, 1527, sio hata miaka miwili tangu upatanisho wake wa jasiri tena, alizama kwenye Mto Limmat uliopita kupitia Zurich. Maneno yake ya mwisho yalikuwa: “Mikononi mwako, Ee Mungu, ninaweka roho yangu.”

Harakati ya Anabaptist ilidumu zaidi ya hawa watatu.

Ilienea na kukua kote Moravia, Uholanzi, Uswisi, na mkoa wa Palatinate wa Ujerumani. Karibu miaka mia moja baadaye kulikuwa kiongozi mwingine mashuhuri katika milima ya Zurich; huyu alikuwa mkulima mzee. Alikuwa na uzoefu wa kuongoza kundi lake kupitia mawimbi na mtiririko wa changamoto zilizo mbele ya waumini wa wakati huo. Jina lake ni Hans Landis.

Mwaka ulikuwa 1613, Januari 26 kwa kuwa sahihi. Waliekusanyika kwenye kastali ndogo, Wadenswil, kando ya Ziwa Zurich, alikuwa Hans Landis mzee, pamoja na wanachama kumi na wanne wa kanisa lake. Miongoni mwao aliyejulikana sana alikuwa Galli Fuchs, mwalimu wa shule na aliyebadilika hivi karibuni, pamoja na Bachman, fundi chuma na mjanja wa vurugu aliyejulikana, ambaye naye alikuwa amebadilika hivi karibuni. Waliokutana nao walikuwa maafisa tisa wa kanisa na serikali, ikiwemo meya wa Zurich, Rudolf Rhan; mkuu wake wa polisi, Conrad Grebel (kinuashiria jina la mtoaji wa ubatizo wa takriban karne moja kabla); na wahubiri kadhaa wa kanisa la Protestant la Zurich. Sababu ya mkutano huu ilikuwa kwamba kazi ya kiroho ya Hans ilikuwa imebarikiwa, na makanisa yake madogo yalikuwa yakiongezeka kwa haraka, yakisababisha mabadiliko katika kuhudhuria makanisa ya mashambani ya kanisa la Protestant. Kupungua kwa kuhudhuria kulileta matatizo kadhaa kwa serikali iliyojumuisha kanisa na serikali.

Kwanza, Kanisa la Protestant lilikusanya fedha nyingi kutoka kwa waumini wake. Hivyo basi, kanisa jingine lililokuwa likivuruga na kubadilisha wanachama wake lilionelewa si tu kama tishio la kiroho, bali pia kama tishio la kifedha. Mikoa ya cantons yalikuwa mara kwa mara yakijihusisha katika mapigano yaliyochochewa na dini, kuanzia mabishano yaliyokasirika hadi kampeni za kijeshi. Pili, mafundisho ya kiroho yanayotofautiana na dini rasmi ya serikali mara nyingi yaliwasilishwa nyakati za vurugu za kiraia, na mapinduzi ya wakulima ya cantons jirani yalikuwa bado katika kumbukumbu za wazee wa eneo na wahubiri. Matukio kama ya Muensterites na tafsiri zao za vurugu za Maandiko yalibaki onyo dhahiri la uzito wa nidhamu ya kidini iliyoenda vibaya. Mapinduzi haya yalitokea wakati Kanisa Katoliki lilipokuwa likianguka katika eneo hilo, jambo lililotengeneza fursa kwa imani mpya na wakati mwingine kali kuchipuka. Sasa, shughuli za Hans na kanisa lake zilionekana kwa maafisa hawa kama jambo lililo karibu na mapinduzi na usaliti.

Mkutano huu haukuwa ni kukutana kwa mara ya kwanza kati ya Hans Landis na kundi lake na mamlaka za mtaa. Uchunguzi wa awali ulifanywa, takriban miaka minne kabla. Ripoti hiyo ilielezea maeneo yao ya kukutana kama misitu, maghala, na hata nyumbani kwa Hans Landis. Hata hivyo, hakuna orodha ya wanachama iliyoingizwa, kwani hata majirani wa Kanisa la Protestant walikataa kumtaja yeyote wa Anabaptists. Sio tu kwamba umma wa eneo ulikataa kushirikiana kwa kumtaja yeyote wa makanisa ya Hans, bali pia kulikuwa na uvumi kwamba Taufer (Anabaptists) walikuwa na mfuko wa jumla, chini ya uendeshaji wa Deacon Jacob Isler, ambao walitumia kugharamia mahitaji ndani ya jamii yao. Kwa maafisa, hili lilionekana kama hila nyingine ya kuwashawishi maskini wa jamii waachane na kanisa lao na kujiunga na Hans na kikundi chake.

Meya Rhan alifungua mkutano, akiwahutubia wale walioshiriki kwa maneno “Mheshimiwa, waliokuwa na elimu nyingi, wenye haki, wenye heshima, wenye busara, (na) ndugu mpendwa.” Kisha, aliwambia Hans na ndugu zake waliokuwamo, akiwapa salamu ya kirafiki ya “Wapendwa, ndugu wazuri na wema” kabla ya kuwaonya kwa kuwataja kama “raia”. Baada ya mbinu hizi zisizo za moja kwa moja, aliwauliza, akitafuta ufafanuzi juu ya “sababu [kwanini] mmelaana na kanisa letu na … kuanzisha sect tofauti.” Kufuatia swali hili, aliwahakikishia kwamba baraza lilitaka kuwa mvumilivu lakini kwamba wategemao wa kutengwa “wasitumiuse udhuru wa uvumilivu na fadhili za mami.”

Kukabiliana na utangulizi huu, Hans aliomba ruhusa kwa yeye na ndugu zake kusimama na kuzungumza na “Mami Wenye Fadhili.” Ilipokubaliwa, alisimama, akimshukuru meya kwa maneno yake ya salamu kabla ya kuuliza nia yao juu ya imani ya Anabaptists, akidai kwamba walikuwa wamewahi kusikia kama hizo hapo awali. Aliongeza kwamba mafundisho yao yote yalikuwa “hakuna kitu tofauti na kile Kristu alifundisha na ambacho mitume waliandika.” Kama hapo awali, Anabaptists waliomba tu kuruhusiwa kushikilia hili, wakiunga mkono serikali zao katika masuala yasiyohusiana na dhamiri. Waliendelea pia kusali kwa ajili ya serikali na viongozi wao.

Meya Rhan hakufurahia jibu hili, akalichukua kama kudai kwamba yeye na Kanisa la Protestant hawakutii maagizo ya Kristo. Hans, baada ya kusikia jibu hili, aliomba ruhusa kuchukua kikundi chake nje ya chumba kwa muda mfupi. Waliporejea, Galli Fuchs aliletwa na kutoa ushuhuda kwa mami, akiweka wazi safari yake ya kiroho kupitia makanisa ya Protestant na Katoliki, akitambua kwamba ingawa wote walihubiri vizuri mbele ya mihadhara, wote pia walikataa mafundisho haya kwa maisha yao yasiyo ya Mungu. Baada ya kusoma imani na utekelezaji wa Anabaptist, Galli alibadilika.

Maafisa walikuwa na shaka, wakidai kwamba hoja za Galli “huzidi kuonyesha hakuna sababu kwa uamuzi wenu wa kutengwa.” Baada ya jibu hili, mtabadilika mwingine aliletwa mbele, huyu alikuwa fundi chuma Bachman. Bachman alitambulika mara moja na Conrad Grebel (si mwanzilishi wa Anabaptist), mkuu wa polisi wa Zurich, kama mmoja wa wachokozi wa mtaa—“Ni kweli, ulikuwa mgeni kwa Mungu [na] hakuna mtu wote katika eneo zima ambaye nilikuwa na shida naye zaidi kuliko wewe.”

Ushuhuda wa Bachman ulirudia puntos nyingi za Galli, hasa kuhusu utsafi na kutengwa kwa kanisa la kweli, ukimalizika na nukuu hii kutoka Sirach: “Yeye asiyechanganya korongo atakuwa amechomwa.”

Mijadala iliendelea, na mzozo ulizuka kuhusu mgawanyo wa sala ya kiroho, mifano ya viongozi wa kanisa, na maarifa ya wokovu. Mkutano ulipomalizika, Galli Fuchs hakuweza kujizuia kutamka tena: “Kama mngewatakia kanisa la Hirzel, … mtaona … nani angekuwa na umati mkubwa zaidi!” Hili lalisababisha vicheko kutoka chumba, na Hans alichukua fursa ya mwisho zaidi ya kuzungumza, akiomba: “Ee mabwana wapenzi, tuende tukashikilie kile tunachoamini.”

Baada ya ombi hili, meya alifikiria, hatimaye akiamua kwamba ndugu zao wangepewa ruhusa ya kuondoka bila kukamatwa, ambao, walipoondoka, walisikika wakisema kwa makubaliano: “Tungependelea pia kutoa uhai, mwili, mali, na damu.” Walikuwa hivi karibuni kupata fursa ya kuishi dhamira hii.

Miaka kumi na tano ilipita. Hans alifungwa gerezani katika mnara wa Wellenberg huko Zurich, pamoja na Galli Fuchs, Deacon Jacob Isler, Hans Meili, Stephen Zehnder, na Paul Degia (mzaliwa wa Milano, Italia). Walishikiliwa kwa wiki kumi na nne huko, na mara kwa mara walisisitizwa, kuulizwa maswali, na kutishiwa. Hatimaye maagizo yalitolewa kwamba wangalazimishwe kuondoka canton ya Zurich, lakini Hans alikataa, kwa hivyo baraza lilijibu na tishio linalochukuliwa kuwa kuu kuliko kifo. Baraza lilidai kwamba kwa sababu ya uasi wa kiraia wa wanaume hawa, sio imani zao, walistahili kuadhibiwa kama watumwa wa meli wa kuoga ili kuendesha meli za Ufaransa katika Bahari ya Mediteranea.

Jacob Isler alimwomba mami, akiwauliza wangeyafanya jinsi hiyo, wakijua kwamba Taufer (Anabaptists) hawawezi kuvumilia kuondoka kwa familia zao. Stephen Zhender aliongeza: “Tusingeogopa kwenda baharini na maji kwa kuwa pia ni uumbaji wa Mungu.” Licha ya maombi haya, baraza lilitimiza vitisho vyake, likiitisha hukumu ya watumwa wa meli kwa wote sita.

Hukumu ilisababisha mshtuko katika jamii. Muda wa kuishi wa mtumwa wa meli mchanga na mwenye afya hauzidi miaka mitatu, na miaka hiyo mitatu ingekuwa imejaa njaa, kuathirika na baridi, kupigwa, na uchovu. Hata katika cantons za Kikatholiki kali, hukumu hii ilikuwa kali. Katika jamii ya Protestant iliyokuwa na upole zaidi, ilisababisha hasira ya umma.

Wafungwa wote walipewa fursa ya mwisho ya kuondoka canton, ambapo watatu kati yao walikubali. Lakini Galli Fuchs, Stephen Zehnder, na Hans Landis walikataa kwa msimamo kubadilisha mawazo yao. Baadaye waliendeshwa kwa walinzi magharibi kuelekea balozi wa Ufaransa huko Solothurn, mji katika canton ya Bern. Bern ilichukua hatua kwa namna ile ile kama Zurich, na zawadi ilitolewa ili kuwaondolea wafungwa. Wakati hilo lilishindikana, faili lilifunguliwa kwa siri seli yao huko Solothurn. Mambo ya kifungo ya wafungwa yalikatwa kwa haraka, na wakatoroka mji, wakikimbia kurejea nyumbani. Walipofika nyumbani, umma, bado ukiukashangazwa na matibabu yao, ulikataa kuwataja kwa mamlaka.

Habari za kutoroka zilienea na kukua, na Hans alikuwapo kazini, akibatiza waliobadilika wapya, na hata kukagua ndoa kadhaa. Anabaptists walistawi, wakiwasaidia maskini wa jamii kwa chakula na mikopo isiyo na riba kutoka kwa mfuko wao wa misaada. Shughuli za upya zilisababisha hasira na hofu kwa maafisa, ambao hatimaye waliamua kwamba juhudi za kiongozi wao mzee zilihitaji kuondolewa.

Hans alikamatwa mara moja baada ya uamuzi huu na tena kufungwa katika Wellenberg. Hapa vitisho na kuonya kutoka kwa mamlaka viliongezeka. Ikiwa hatang'unguiwi au hata kuondoka canton, wangekuwa wanamzima.

Vitisho kama hivi havikumutetega Hans. Badala yake, alimwambia mami wasifanye dhambi katika kuwahudumia yeye, akithibitisha nia yake kwamba alikuwa “amemkabidhi mwenyewe kwa Mungu” na “ alikuwa tayari kusubiri kile Mungu atakayomletea.”

Diehe hali ya ujasiri wa Hans ilileta utambuzi sawa kwa maafisa: wangetakiwa kutimiza vitisho vyao. Walimchukulia Hans kama msaliti, walisema kwamba alikuwa “anataka kuwa mwenye bwana wake bila kujali mamlaka waliyoheshimika,” na kwamba alionyesha “upinzani mgumu, wa uasi wa watu wabaya.” Licha ya madai haya pamoja na vitisho vyao, makatibu walitambua kwamba utekelezaji wa adhabu ungekuwa jambo lisilopendwa. Hans aliheshimiwa sana na umma wa mtaa, na hata alikuwa na uhusiano Amsterdam, ambapo binti yake aliishi, aliyekuwa ameolewa kwa Mennonite wa Kiuda.

Afisa Grebel, wahubiri wa Protestant, na wengine walitoa muda mwingi kujadili na Hans katika seli yake ya gereza, lakini hawakufanikiwa. Kufikia Alhamisi, Septemba 29, 1614, waligundua kuwa hakuwa rahisi kubadilika katika imani yake, hakutaka kukataa wala kuondoka canton. Ripoti hii, iliyowasilishwa kwa mami, iliwaleta kwenye majadiliano makubwa. Wengine walipendekeza kumkata sikio Hans hadharani na kumtupa nje, wakati wengine waliona kifungo cha maisha kama adhabu inayofaa zaidi. Jambo hilo likapitishwa kwa kupiga kura saa sita mchana, na mwamuzi wa wengi ukafikiwa haraka. Hans Landis angechinjwa hadharani mara moja.

Hans, aliposikia uamuzi huo, alidhani ni mbinu nyingine tu ya kumshawishi kukataa. Hata hivyo, alipokaribia eneo la kutendewa adhabu ambalo lilijulikana mjini Zurich, uso wake ukaiva njano, na mikono yake ikamfikia kichwa. Hata hivyo, alijirefusha haraka, akitabasamu na kuwaonya umati wasilie, kwani alikuwa na matumaini mema. Akimwona mkewe na watoto wake walikuwepo, aliwaomba waondoke ili nia yake isidhurike.

Adhabu ilisomwa; Hans alisimama kimya. Hakuna neno la lawama lililolalamikiwa dhidi ya maadili yake binafsi. Badala yake, suala lilikuwa kukataa kwake kubomoa kanisa lake. Alibaki thabiti, na hivyo mchongaji wa kifo, Paul Vollmar, alimpeleka Hans hadi eneo la utekelezaji. Watu waliotazama walidai Vollmar alimwachia Hans, akimpa njia ya kutoroka. Wakati Hans hakufanya hivyo, Vollmar alimwinua mikono kwake kwa Mungu, akiomba msamaha kwa kile sheria ilimlazimu afanye. Hans, akitabasamu, alisema msamaha kwa mtu huyo, wakati wahubiri mbalimbali walimshawishi amkatae, lakini Hans alijibu kwamba hakumuona toba ndani yao.

Vollmar, alipofika mahali pa utekelezaji, alimpa Hans nafasi ya kuzungumza bila kuingiliwa, na Hans alizungumza kwa kifupi tu: “Sijui ni nini zaidi nichukue kusema isipokuwa nataka kila mtu afahamu dhambi zao na ateremke, ili waokolewe; hili ningelitaka kwa kila mtu.”

Kisha, ndani ya mwonekano wa mahali ambapo Feliz Manz alitoa maisha yake karibia karne moja iliyopita, alikanyaga magoti na kukunja kichwa chake. Upanga ulipiga chini kwa mwangaza, kisha Paul Vollmar aliuliza swali la utaratibu: “Je, nimekamatwa mtu huyu kwa usahihi?”

“Ndiyo,” jibu liliwahi, “umekamataa mtu huyu maskini.”

Mwathiriwa wa uamuzi wa ujasiri wa mzee Hans ulisababisha kongamano la msaada na hasira katika jamii isiyo ya Anabaptist. Rhudlof Rhan na Conrad Grebel waliendelea kumsukuma Anabaptists waliobaki, wakaweka Margaretha Landis, mpwa wa Hans, katika kifungo cha pekee hospitalini baada ya kukataa kufuata matakwa yao. Watoto wa Hans nao walibaki imara wakikataa kukataa, lakini wajukuu kadhaa wa Hans walianza kuhudhuria kanisa la jiji muda mfupi baada ya utekelezaji wa babu yao.

Kikundi cha Anabaptist cha mtaa kilibaki imara pia. Wazao wake kiroho wangebeba neno la Kristo nao wakati, karne moja baadaye, uhamiaji mkubwa ulipowaleta kwenye fukwe zenye mwitu za Ulimwengu Mpya. Hapa, katika uhuru wa kidini wa Pennsylvania, wangeanzisha jamii mpya ambapo imani iliyogharimu Hans Landis maisha yake ilikua kwa vizazi vijavyo. Leo, kuna waumini kote Amerika ambao wanajitahidi kuishi imani yao kwa mujibu wa dhamiri yao, ambao wako pale walipo kwa sababu ya maisha yaliyopatikana na Hans miaka karibu 400 iliyopita. Wengine ni wazao wake, na wengine ni marafiki wa wazao wake. Mungu atutusukume kutembea kama Yesu alivyotembea, kama Hans alivyo.

“Why don’t we have a cure for cancer yet?” My patient asked me.

I shrugged. “There are lots of different kinds of cancer,” I said. “For some, there are cures, while for others we are still learning how best to treat them.”

“I think,” my patient said with the confidence that he was supposedly sharing a top-secret theory. “I think there actually is a cure for cancer, but the drug companies just don’t want us to know about it.”

I shook my head. “I think we are doing the best we can,” I told him. “We’ve come a long way when it comes to treatment of cancer, but we still have a long way to go.”

Cancer is a scary illness. One Christian man told me that he wasn’t afraid of dying, but if he had a choice, he would choose almost any other way to go than to die of cancer.

More than that, it is something that seems mysterious. More people seem to be getting it, yet no one really knows why.

In this article, I would like to take some time to explore what cancer is, and to discuss cancer screening tests. In the second part (in the next issue) Lord willing, I will discuss some of the treatments available for cancers.

I will mention here that I am a family doctor. I have cared for many patients with cancer, but I am certainly not an oncologist, nor do I know everything about cancer. What I understand, I am willing to share.

What is Cancer?

As with many things, we can trace the beginnings of cancer back to the fall of man in the Garden of Eden. We know that God created humans perfectly. As originally created, not only did they not have cancer, but they also would not have gotten it either.

In order to understand what cancer is, we need to understand how normal tissue and cells behave.

Normal cells live for a period of time and then die. This process is called apoptosis. It makes certain that there is a constant turnover of cells. It also prevents one type of cell from getting “out of line” and beginning to grow in a place where it doesn’t belong.

Every time our cells divide, they copy their DNA into the daughter cells. Usually this happens without error, but occasionally there is an error in the copy process. We call these errors mutations.

Cancer cells are cells that have lost the normal brakes on their behavior. Because of mutations in their DNA, they no longer have a limited life span, nor do they observe the limits of where they belong within the body. Instead, they begin to encroach on surrounding tissues, pulling in additional blood supply and nutrients in the process.

Cancer cells can enlarge locally, or they can spread through the lymphatic system or circulatory system to distant parts of the body. When cancer cells end up in other locations than where they originated, we call it metastases.

The type of cancer is determined by the type of cell that is multiplying out of control. Doctors don’t generally talk about “skin cancer,” even though there are cancers that originate in skin cells. Instead, they classify these cancers into basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma—each one referring to a different kind of skin cell. Each one of these skin cancers acts differently. Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma get bigger in a local area and seldom spread elsewhere, while melanoma is very prone to spreading to other parts of the body.

Additionally, how a cancer responds to treatment is going to be based on the type of cell that it comes from, not simply the organ where it originates.

Causes of Mutations…

We do not know how common cancer was in the days before the flood. I would speculate that it was fairly rare.

We know that before the flood, men lived to be very old—often into their 900s. Mutations must have been rare. Their DNA was closer to the original genetic specimen of mankind (and thus, to perfection) than ours is in the 21st century (AD) Therefore, the chance of genes mutating and abnormal genes popping up was much less than it is now.

…Environmental Factors

Beyond that, something must have happened around the time of the flood that increased the rate of mutations. Perhaps there was an increase in radiation levels. Maybe there were genetic changes that gradually caused cancer to show up.

Cancer is not mentioned in the Bible, although it is possible that Hezekiah’s “boil” could have been some kind of cancerous growth. It is also possible that some of the diseases that affected the Philistines when the ark of the covenant was in their land were cancerous tumors.

People began dying at younger ages after the flood and by soon after the time of Abraham, they were seldom living much past their one hundredth year.

Today, we know that things which damage a cell’s copying mechanism and its DNA increase the risk of cancer. The most well-known of these is radiation.

After the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, survivors were noted to have significant increases in certain kinds of cancer. Leukemia (cancer of the blood) was the most common type of cancer, followed by cancer of stomach, lung, liver, and breast.

Radiation isn’t something that most people deal with on a regular basis. However, if you work in an x-ray department or if you needed to have radiation to treat some type of cancer, it is possible that you have been exposed to much higher levels of radiation than the general public.

There are plenty of other things that are associated with increases in cancers. Exposure to ultraviolet light increases the risk of skin cancer and is a big reason why doctors recommend sunscreen and protective clothing while enjoying the sunshine to limit ultraviolet exposure.

Finally, there are plenty of chemicals that are present in different types of work that can increase the risk of cancer.

…Unhealthy Foods

Foods that are high in nitrites increase the risk of intestinal cancers. Nitrites are typically present in smoked and cured meats. So, to be healthy, people should limit their intake of these foods to none or at the very least, a very limited percentage of the overall diet.

…Certain Prior Diseases

Another thing to mention is that certain types of infections can increase the risk of cancer. Epstein Barr virus, which causes infectious mononucleosis, has been associated with certain kinds of lymphoma. Hepatitis B and C increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). And Helicobacter pylori infections in the stomach are associated with stomach cancers.

It is important to remember that just because someone has had one of these viruses it will not necessarily cause them to get cancer from that infection. Rather, it simply increases the risk that the person infected will get cancer at some point in the future.

…Unhealthy Habits

One last thing to mention is that certain toxins dramatically increase the risk of cancer. An obvious one is tobacco use, which strongly increases the risk of lung cancer, throat cancer, and even bladder cancer. Alcohol is another risk factor. Alcohol increases the risk of mouth and throat cancers, gastrointestinal cancers, and liver cancer. There really isn’t a safe amount of exposure to either of these toxic agents, but certainly the higher the level of exposure, the worse it is.

Screening for Cancer

There are many tests available that claim to be able to screen for a variety of cancers. Most of them are at least a little effective at identifying cancers at an early stage. However, there are a few problems with some of them which indicate that a certain test is ineffective at truly helping with the screening process.

A good place to start is to simply think about what a perfect screening test would look like. This will help us to see where tests might be beneficial or not.

A perfect screening test is going to have a number of features. First, it will have no false positive or false negative results. In other words, everyone who tests positive with the test will have cancer and those who test negative will not have cancer. Next, the test will identify the cancer at a point early enough in its development that it is easy to treat. The test will be cheap and minimally invasive, and it will require minimal exposure to radiation.

Unfortunately, no test that we currently do for screening totally meets these criteria.

For one thing, many tests produce both false positive and negative tests. These are both problems. The issue with a false negative test is obvious—it leads to someone thinking they don’t have cancer when they really do. A false positive test on the other hand leads to higher anxiety levels along with the cost and dangers from whatever ongoing testing is necessary to let a patient know that they don’t really have cancer.

An example of a bad test, in this respect, is the CEA-125. CEA-125 is a chemical that is made by some types of cancer. Oncologists use this level to track a patient’s response to chemotherapy.

It would make sense that you could use this as a screening test for these cancers, but it simply doesn’t work. Many people have elevated CEA levels, even though they don’t have cancer and on the other side, plenty of GI (gastrointestinal) cancers don’t make this chemical at all. Testing lots of people with CEA-125 testing will lead to more scans and biopsies, but it is doubtful if it would have a significant impact on death rates from cancer.

Another issue has to do with a particular cancer itself. In order for a test to be helpful, the cancer needs to have a long progression through precancerous stages until finally it develops into full-blown cancer.

An example is colon cancer. Most people who develop colon cancer have precancerous polyps several years before they get the cancer. This is why colonoscopies can be effective at preventing the progression to colon cancer.

If a patient has a colonoscopy, the doctor can detect the presence of polyps. More than that, he can remove the polyps through the scope, hopefully stopping the progression to cancer.

One last, related point is that there needs to be some benefit to early detection of cancer. If a new test can detect cancer six months earlier than existing tests, people will live an average of six months longer with the cancer than before, even if nothing else changes.

The question is whether diagnosing the cancer earlier leads to more effective treatment. Can you take it out before it spreads to the lymph glands and thereby completely avoid the need for chemotherapy?

If treatment and response rates are the same regardless of the stage at which you diagnose a cancer, then screening doesn’t really make sense.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force is a volunteer panel of experts that have reviewed the literature on a variety of tests. Based on the studies that have been conducted regarding the available tests, they make recommendations about the various tests and how often to use them.

This panel tends to be more conservative in their recommendations than many cancer societies. For instance, they recommend every other year for the use of mammograms for women between the ages of 50 and 75, as compared to the yearly screening recommended by other groups.

With each recommendation they give a grade of how good the studies are which support that specific recommendation, along with links for those studies. Their recommendations are well researched. This is helpful for low-risk people trying to decide what testing to do. If someone has a high risk because of family history or exposures, their recommendations are less helpful.

Cancer Challenges

People often discuss cancer as though it was a single entity. As before mentioned, cancer is not just one thing. Skin cancer behaves differently from lymphoma, which in turn behaves differently from sarcomas. The chance that there will ever be a single treatment for all cancer—the “Cure for Cancer” which people talk about, is unlikely.

An even bigger challenge when dealing with cancer cells is that they are very similar to our normal cells. Basically, we are trying to poison the cancer just a little more than the rest of our normal tissues. There are a number of different treatments that are currently available. In Part 2, we will address some of the different options available today and some others that may become available in the future.

Final Thoughts

There are a few things that come to mind when contemplating the subject of cancer.

We do not need to live in fear or make choices out of fear. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness –Isaiah 41:10.

I don’t think that we should fatalistically allow anything to happen that might, simply because it is “God’s will.” We need to make wise choices, then having done so, we should not live in a state of anxiety.

Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Matthew 6:31-34.

Finally, if we can, through wise decisions, prevent a certain cancer from forming or spreading, that seems like a reasonable goal. None of us will live forever in this body, but if we can die of something other than cancer, that seems like a good goal too. May God give us wisdom to care for the body which He has given us.

“왜 아직까지 암 치료제가 없는 거죠?” 내 환자가 나에게 물었다.

나는 어깨를 으쓱했다. “암에는 여러 종류가 있습니다.”라고 말했다. “어떤 암은 치료법이 있지만, 다른 암들은 아직 어떻게 가장 잘 치료할지 배우는 중입니다.”

“제 생각에는,” 내 환자는 자신이 일급 비밀 이론을 전하는 것 같은 확신을 가지고 말했다. “사실 암에 대한 치료법이 있는데 제약회사들이 우리에게 알리고 싶어하지 않는 것 같아요.”

나는 머리를 저었다. “우리는 최선을 다하고 있다고 생각합니다.”라고 그에게 말했다. “암 치료에 관해서는 많은 진전이 있었지만, 아직도 갈 길이 멉니다.”

암은 무서운 병이다. 한 기독교 남성은 죽는 것을 두려워하지는 않지만, 만약 선택권이 있다면 암으로 죽는 것보다는 거의 어떤 다른 방식으로 죽는 편을 택하겠다고 말했다.

그보다 더한 것은 암이 신비롭게 보인다는 점이다. 암에 걸리는 사람이 더 많은 것처럼 보이지만, 아무도 정확히 이유를 모르는 것 같다.

이 글에서는 암이 무엇인지, 그리고 암 선별검사에 관해 살펴보려고 한다. 다음 호에서(주님이 허락하신다면) 암에 대해 사용 가능한 치료법들 가운데 몇 가지를 논의하겠다.

여기에서 밝히자면 나는 가정의학과 의사다. 나는 암 환자들을 많이 돌보아 왔지만, 결코 종양학자(온콜로지스트)는 아니며 암에 대해 모든 것을 아는 것도 아니다. 내가 이해하는 바를 기꺼이 나누겠다.

암이란 무엇인가?

많은 것들과 마찬가지로, 우리는 암의 기원을 에덴 동산에서 인간의 타락으로 거슬러 올라가 설명할 수 있다. 하나님은 사람을 완전하게 창조하셨음을 우리는 안다. 원래 창조된 상태에서는 암이 없었을 뿐만 아니라 암에 걸리지도 않았을 것이다.

암이 무엇인지 이해하려면 정상 조직과 세포가 어떻게 행동하는지를 이해해야 한다.

정상 세포는 일정 기간 살아 있다가 죽는다. 이 과정을 세포자멸사(apoptosis)라고 한다. 이것은 세포가 지속적으로 교체되도록 보장한다. 또한 하나의 세포 유형이 “선을 넘어” 제자리에 있지 않은 곳에서 증식하는 것을 막는다.

세포가 분열할 때마다 DNA를 딸세포에게 복사한다. 보통은 오류 없이 이루어지지만 가끔 복사 과정에서 오류가 발생한다. 우리는 이러한 오류를 돌연변이라고 부른다.

암세포는 정상적인 행동에 대한 제동을 잃은 세포들이다. DNA의 돌연변이 때문에 이들은 더 이상 한정된 수명을 갖지 않으며 자신이 몸의 어디에 있어야 하는지의 경계를 지키지 않는다. 대신 주변 조직을 침범하기 시작하고 그 과정에서 추가적인 혈액 공급과 영양분을 끌어들인다.

암세포는 국소적으로 커질 수 있고, 림프계나 순환계를 통해 몸의 먼 부위로 퍼질 수 있다. 암세포가 원래 발생한 장소가 아닌 다른 위치로 옮겨간 경우 우리는 그것을 전이(metastases)라고 부른다.

암의 유형은 통제 불능으로 증식하는 세포의 종류에 의해 결정된다. 의사들은 일반적으로 “피부암”이라고만 말하지 않는다. 피부 세포에서 시작하는 암들이 있긴 하지만, 대신 이러한 암들을 기저세포암(basal cell carcinoma), 편평세포암(squamous cell carcinoma), 흑색종(melanoma)으로 분류한다—각각이 다른 종류의 피부 세포를 가리킨다. 이들 각 피부암은 서로 다르게 행동한다. 기저세포암과 편평세포암은 국소 부위에서 커지고 거의 다른 곳으로 퍼지지 않는 반면, 흑색종은 다른 부위로 전이될 가능성이 매우 높다.

또한, 암이 치료에 어떻게 반응하는지는 단순히 발생한 장기에 의해서가 아니라 그것이 유래한 세포 유형에 의해 좌우된다.

돌연변이의 원인…

홍수 이전 시대에 암이 얼마나 흔했는지는 알 수 없다. 나는 비교적 드물었을 것이라고 추측한다.

우리는 홍수 이전에 사람들이 매우 오래 살았다는 것을 안다—종종 900년대까지 살았다. 돌연변이는 드물었음에 틀림없다. 그들의 DNA는 원래 인류의 유전적 표본(따라서 완전성)에 더 가까웠으며, 우리 21세기(서기) 사람들보다 더 완전에 가까웠다. 따라서 유전자가 돌연변이로 변하고 비정상적인 유전자가 생겨날 확률은 지금보다 훨씬 적었다.

…환경적 요인

그보다 더하여, 홍수 무렵에 돌연변이율을 증가시킨 무언가가 있었을 것이다. 어쩌면 방사선 수치가 증가했을 수도 있다. 아마도 암이 점차 나타나도록 하는 유전적 변화들이 있었을지도 모른다.

성경에는 암이 직접적으로 언급되어 있지 않지만, 히스기야의 “종기”가 어떤 종류의 암성 성장일 가능성도 있다. 또한 언약궤가 블레셋 땅에 있을 때 블레셋 사람들에게 영향을 미쳤던 어떤 질병들이 암성 종양이었을 가능성도 있다.

사람들은 홍수 이후 더 젊은 나이에 죽기 시작했고, 아브라함 시대 직후에는 거의 백세를 넘기지 못했다.

오늘날 우리는 세포의 복제 기계와 DNA를 손상시키는 것들이 암 위험을 증가시킨다는 것을 알고 있다. 그중 가장 잘 알려진 것은 방사선이다.

히로시마와 나가사키에 원자폭탄이 투하된 후 생존자들에게서 특정 종류의 암이 크게 증가한 것이 관찰되었다. 백혈병(혈액의 암)이 가장 흔한 유형이었고, 그 다음으로 위암, 폐암, 간암, 유방암이 뒤를 이었다.

방사선은 대부분의 사람들이 일상적으로 접하는 것은 아니다. 그러나 엑스레이 부서에서 일하거나 어떤 종류의 암을 치료하기 위해 방사선 치료를 받았던 경우, 일반 대중보다 훨씬 높은 수준의 방사선에 노출되었을 가능성이 있다.

암 증가와 관련된 다른 요인들도 많이 있다. 자외선 노출은 피부암 위험을 높이며, 그래서 의사들이 햇볕을 즐길 때 자외선 노출을 제한하기 위해 자외선 차단제와 보호복을 권장하는 큰 이유 중 하나다.

마지막으로, 다양한 작업 환경에서 존재하는 많은 화학물질들이 암 위험을 증가시킬 수 있다.

…건강에 해로운 음식

질산염(nitrites)이 많이 함유된 음식은 장(腸) 암의 위험을 증가시킨다. 질산염은 일반적으로 훈제 및 가공육에 존재한다. 따라서 건강을 위해 사람들은 이러한 음식의 섭취를 전혀 하지 않거나 적어도 전체 식단에서 매우 제한된 비율로 제한해야 한다.

…특정한 이전 질병들

또 한 가지 언급할 것은 특정 유형의 감염이 암 위험을 증가시킬 수 있다는 점이다. 전염성 단핵구증을 일으키는 엡스타인-바 바이러스는 특정 종류의 림프종과 관련이 있다. B형 및 C형 간염은 간세포암(간암)의 위험을 높인다. 위의 헬리코박터 파일로리 감염은 위암과 연관되어 있다.

이러한 바이러스 중 하나를 가지고 있었다고 해서 반드시 그 감염으로 인해 암에 걸리는 것은 아니라는 점을 기억하는 것이 중요하다. 오히려 단지 그 사람에게 미래 어느 시점에 암이 발생할 위험을 높일 뿐이다.

…건강에 해로운 습관

마지막으로 언급할 것은 특정 독소들이 암 위험을 극적으로 증가시킨다는 것이다. 명백한 예는 담배 사용으로, 폐암, 인후암, 심지어 방광암의 위험을 강하게 증가시킨다. 알코올도 또 다른 위험 요인이다. 알코올은 구강 및 인후암, 위장관 암, 간암의 위험을 높인다. 이러한 독성 물질에 대한 안전한 노출량은 사실상 없지만, 확실히 노출 정도가 높을수록 더 나쁘다.

암 선별검사

다양한 암을 선별할 수 있다고 주장하는 많은 검사들이 있다. 이들 대부분은 적어도 암을 조기 발견하는 데 어느 정도 효과가 있다. 그러나 일부 검사에는 특정 문제가 있어 그 검사가 실제로 선별 과정에 도움이 되지 못함을 시사한다.

좋은 출발점은 완벽한 선별검사가 어떤 모습일지를 생각해 보는 것이다. 이는 어떤 검사가 유익할지 또는 그렇지 않을지를 판단하는 데 도움이 된다.

완벽한 선별검사는 여러 특징을 갖는다. 첫째, 위양성(false positive)이나 위음성(false negative) 결과가 전혀 없어야 한다. 다시 말해, 검사에서 양성인 모든 사람은 암이 있어야 하고 음성인 사람은 암이 없어야 한다. 다음으로, 검사는 암이 치료하기 쉬운 단계에서 이를 식별해야 한다. 검사는 저렴하고 최소한의 침습적이어야 하며 방사선 노출도 최소화해야 한다.

불행히도 우리가 현재 선별용으로 시행하는 어떤 검사도 이러한 기준을 완전히 충족하지는 못한다.

한 가지 이유는 많은 검사들이 위양성과 위음성 결과를 모두 산출한다는 점이다. 이 둘은 모두 문제다. 위음성 검사의 문제는 명백하다—실제로 암이 있는데도 암이 없다고 생각하게 만든다. 반면 위양성 검사는 더 높은 불안 수준과 환자에게 암이 실제로 없다는 것을 확인하기 위해 필요한 추가 검사들의 비용과 위험을 초래한다.

이와 관련해 나쁜 예의 하나는 CEA-125이다. CEA-125는 일부 유형의 암이 만들어내는 화학물질이다. 종양학자들은 화학요법에 대한 환자의 반응을 추적하기 위해 이 수치를 사용한다.

이것을 이러한 암들에 대한 선별검사로 사용할 수 있을 것 같지만, 단순히 작동하지 않는다. 암이 없음에도 불구하고 CEA 수치가 상승해 있는 사람이 많고 반대로 많은 위장관(GI) 암은 전혀 이 화학물질을 만들지 않는다. 많은 사람들을 대상으로 CEA-125 검사를 하면 스캔과 생검이 더 많이 이루어지겠지만, 암으로 인한 사망률에 상당한 영향을 미칠지는 의문이다.

또 다른 문제는 특정 암 자체와 관련이 있다. 검사가 도움이 되려면 암이 전암 단계들(precancerous stages)을 거치며 오랜 기간에 걸쳐 진행되어야 한다.

예로 대장암이 있다. 대장암이 발생하는 대부분의 사람들은 암이 생기기 수년 전에 전암성 용종을 가지고 있다. 이 때문에 대장내시경은 대장암으로의 진행을 예방하는 데 효과적일 수 있다.

환자가 대장내시경을 받으면 의사는 용종의 존재를 감지할 수 있다. 더 나아가, 내시경을 통해 용종을 제거할 수 있어 암으로의 진행을 멈출 수 있다.

마지막으로 관련된 점은 조기 발견에 이득이 있어야 한다는 것이다. 만약 새로운 검사가 기존 검사보다 암을 6개월 더 일찍 발견할 수 있다면, 다른 것이 변하지 않더라도 사람들은 평균적으로 암과 함께 6개월 더 오래 살게 된다.

문제는 암을 더 일찍 진단하는 것이 더 효과적인 치료로 이어지는가이다. 림프절로 퍼지기 전에 암을 제거할 수 있어 화학요법의 필요를 완전히 피할 수 있는가?

치료와 반응률이 암을 진단하는 단계에 관계없이 동일하다면, 선별검사는 실제로 의미가 없다.

미국예방서비스 태스크포스(United States Preventive Services Task Force)는 다양한 검사에 관한 문헌을 검토한 전문가 자원봉사 패널이다. 이용 가능한 검사들에 대해 수행된 연구들을 바탕으로 이들은 다양한 검사와 검사 시행 빈도에 대한 권고를 제시한다.

이 패널은 많은 암 학회들보다 권고에서 더 보수적인 경향이 있다. 예를 들어, 이들은 50세에서 75세 사이의 여성에게 유방촬영술(맘모그램)을 격년(2년마다) 권장하는 반면 다른 단체들은 매년 선별을 권장한다.

각 권고에는 특정 권고를 뒷받침하는 연구들의 수준에 대한 등급과 그 연구들에 대한 링크가 있다. 그들의 권고는 잘 조사되어 있다. 이것은 저위험군 사람이 어떤 검사를 할지 결정하는 데 도움이 된다. 가족력이나 노출 때문에 고위험군인 사람에게는 이들의 권고가 덜 도움이 된다.

암이 주는 도전들

사람들은 종종 암을 하나의 실체인 것처럼 논의한다. 앞서 언급했듯이 암은 단 하나의 것이 아니다. 피부암은 림프종과 다르게 행동하고, 림프종은 결합조직암(sarcoma)과 또 다르게 행동한다. 사람들이 말하는 “암에 대한 단 하나의 치료(암 치료제)”가 언젠가 나올 가능성은 낮다.

암세포를 다루는 데 있어 더 큰 도전은 이들이 정상 세포와 매우 유사하다는 점이다. 기본적으로 우리는 정상 조직보다 암을 조금 더 독살하려고 시도하고 있다. 현재 사용 가능한 다양한 치료법들이 존재한다. 2부에서는 오늘날 이용 가능한 몇 가지 선택지와 미래에 나올 수 있는 다른 선택지들을 다루겠다.

마지막 생각들

암이라는 주제를 생각할 때 몇 가지 떠오르는 점이 있다.

우리는 두려움 속에 살거나 두려움 때문에 선택을 내릴 필요가 없다. 두려워하지 말라 내가 너와 함께 함이라 놀라지 말라 나는 네 하나님이 됨이라 내가 너를 굳세게 하리라 참으로 내가 너를 도우리라 참으로 나의 의로운 오른손으로 너를 붙들리라—이사야 41:10.

나는 우리가 단순히 ‘하나님의 뜻’이니 해서 어떤 일이 일어나도록 운명론적으로 내버려 두어야 한다고 생각하지 않는다. 우리는 지혜로운 선택을 해야 하고, 그러고 나서는 불안 상태에 살지 않아야 한다.

그러므로 무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까 무엇을 입을까 염려하지 말라(저희는 다 이방인들이 구하는 것들이니라) 너희 하늘 아버지께서는 너희가 이 모든 것이 있어야 할 줄을 아시느니라 오직 너희는 먼저 그의 나라와 그의 의를 구하라 그리하면 이 모든 것을 너희에게 더하시리라 그러므로 내일 일을 위하여 염려하지 말라 내일 일은 내일 염려할 것이요 각 날의 괴로움은 그 날에 족하니라—마태복음 6:31-34.

마지막으로, 우리가 지혜로운 결정으로 특정 암이 형성되거나 퍼지는 것을 예방할 수 있다면, 그것은 합리적인 목표처럼 보인다. 우리 누구도 이 몸 안에서 영원히 살지는 못하겠지만, 만약 우리가 암이 아닌 다른 무엇으로 죽을 수 있다면 그것도 좋은 목표인 것 같다. 하나님께서 우리에게 주신 몸을 돌보는 지혜를 우리에게 주시기를 바란다.

“Why don’t we have a cure for cancer yet?” My patient asked me.

I shrugged. “There are lots of different kinds of cancer,” I said. “For some, there are cures, while for others we are still learning how best to treat them.”

“I think,” my patient said with the confidence that he was supposedly sharing a top-secret theory. “I think there actually is a cure for cancer, but the drug companies just don’t want us to know about it.”

I shook my head. “I think we are doing the best we can,” I told him. “We’ve come a long way when it comes to treatment of cancer, but we still have a long way to go.”

Cancer is a scary illness. One Christian man told me that he wasn’t afraid of dying, but if he had a choice, he would choose almost any other way to go than to die of cancer.

More than that, it is something that seems mysterious. More people seem to be getting it, yet no one really knows why.

In this article, I would like to take some time to explore what cancer is, and to discuss cancer screening tests. In the second part (in the next issue) Lord willing, I will discuss some of the treatments available for cancers.

I will mention here that I am a family doctor. I have cared for many patients with cancer, but I am certainly not an oncologist, nor do I know everything about cancer. What I understand, I am willing to share.

What is Cancer?

As with many things, we can trace the beginnings of cancer back to the fall of man in the Garden of Eden. We know that God created humans perfectly. As originally created, not only did they not have cancer, but they also would not have gotten it either.

In order to understand what cancer is, we need to understand how normal tissue and cells behave.

Normal cells live for a period of time and then die. This process is called apoptosis. It makes certain that there is a constant turnover of cells. It also prevents one type of cell from getting “out of line” and beginning to grow in a place where it doesn’t belong.

Every time our cells divide, they copy their DNA into the daughter cells. Usually this happens without error, but occasionally there is an error in the copy process. We call these errors mutations.

Cancer cells are cells that have lost the normal brakes on their behavior. Because of mutations in their DNA, they no longer have a limited life span, nor do they observe the limits of where they belong within the body. Instead, they begin to encroach on surrounding tissues, pulling in additional blood supply and nutrients in the process.

Cancer cells can enlarge locally, or they can spread through the lymphatic system or circulatory system to distant parts of the body. When cancer cells end up in other locations than where they originated, we call it metastases.

The type of cancer is determined by the type of cell that is multiplying out of control. Doctors don’t generally talk about “skin cancer,” even though there are cancers that originate in skin cells. Instead, they classify these cancers into basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma—each one referring to a different kind of skin cell. Each one of these skin cancers acts differently. Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma get bigger in a local area and seldom spread elsewhere, while melanoma is very prone to spreading to other parts of the body.

Additionally, how a cancer responds to treatment is going to be based on the type of cell that it comes from, not simply the organ where it originates.

Causes of Mutations…

We do not know how common cancer was in the days before the flood. I would speculate that it was fairly rare.

We know that before the flood, men lived to be very old—often into their 900s. Mutations must have been rare. Their DNA was closer to the original genetic specimen of mankind (and thus, to perfection) than ours is in the 21st century (AD) Therefore, the chance of genes mutating and abnormal genes popping up was much less than it is now.

…Environmental Factors

Beyond that, something must have happened around the time of the flood that increased the rate of mutations. Perhaps there was an increase in radiation levels. Maybe there were genetic changes that gradually caused cancer to show up.

Cancer is not mentioned in the Bible, although it is possible that Hezekiah’s “boil” could have been some kind of cancerous growth. It is also possible that some of the diseases that affected the Philistines when the ark of the covenant was in their land were cancerous tumors.

People began dying at younger ages after the flood and by soon after the time of Abraham, they were seldom living much past their one hundredth year.

Today, we know that things which damage a cell’s copying mechanism and its DNA increase the risk of cancer. The most well-known of these is radiation.

After the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, survivors were noted to have significant increases in certain kinds of cancer. Leukemia (cancer of the blood) was the most common type of cancer, followed by cancer of stomach, lung, liver, and breast.

Radiation isn’t something that most people deal with on a regular basis. However, if you work in an x-ray department or if you needed to have radiation to treat some type of cancer, it is possible that you have been exposed to much higher levels of radiation than the general public.

There are plenty of other things that are associated with increases in cancers. Exposure to ultraviolet light increases the risk of skin cancer and is a big reason why doctors recommend sunscreen and protective clothing while enjoying the sunshine to limit ultraviolet exposure.

Finally, there are plenty of chemicals that are present in different types of work that can increase the risk of cancer.

…Unhealthy Foods

Foods that are high in nitrites increase the risk of intestinal cancers. Nitrites are typically present in smoked and cured meats. So, to be healthy, people should limit their intake of these foods to none or at the very least, a very limited percentage of the overall diet.

…Certain Prior Diseases

Another thing to mention is that certain types of infections can increase the risk of cancer. Epstein Barr virus, which causes infectious mononucleosis, has been associated with certain kinds of lymphoma. Hepatitis B and C increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). And Helicobacter pylori infections in the stomach are associated with stomach cancers.

It is important to remember that just because someone has had one of these viruses it will not necessarily cause them to get cancer from that infection. Rather, it simply increases the risk that the person infected will get cancer at some point in the future.

…Unhealthy Habits

One last thing to mention is that certain toxins dramatically increase the risk of cancer. An obvious one is tobacco use, which strongly increases the risk of lung cancer, throat cancer, and even bladder cancer. Alcohol is another risk factor. Alcohol increases the risk of mouth and throat cancers, gastrointestinal cancers, and liver cancer. There really isn’t a safe amount of exposure to either of these toxic agents, but certainly the higher the level of exposure, the worse it is.

Screening for Cancer

There are many tests available that claim to be able to screen for a variety of cancers. Most of them are at least a little effective at identifying cancers at an early stage. However, there are a few problems with some of them which indicate that a certain test is ineffective at truly helping with the screening process.

A good place to start is to simply think about what a perfect screening test would look like. This will help us to see where tests might be beneficial or not.

A perfect screening test is going to have a number of features. First, it will have no false positive or false negative results. In other words, everyone who tests positive with the test will have cancer and those who test negative will not have cancer. Next, the test will identify the cancer at a point early enough in its development that it is easy to treat. The test will be cheap and minimally invasive, and it will require minimal exposure to radiation.

Unfortunately, no test that we currently do for screening totally meets these criteria.

For one thing, many tests produce both false positive and negative tests. These are both problems. The issue with a false negative test is obvious—it leads to someone thinking they don’t have cancer when they really do. A false positive test on the other hand leads to higher anxiety levels along with the cost and dangers from whatever ongoing testing is necessary to let a patient know that they don’t really have cancer.

An example of a bad test, in this respect, is the CEA-125. CEA-125 is a chemical that is made by some types of cancer. Oncologists use this level to track a patient’s response to chemotherapy.

It would make sense that you could use this as a screening test for these cancers, but it simply doesn’t work. Many people have elevated CEA levels, even though they don’t have cancer and on the other side, plenty of GI (gastrointestinal) cancers don’t make this chemical at all. Testing lots of people with CEA-125 testing will lead to more scans and biopsies, but it is doubtful if it would have a significant impact on death rates from cancer.

Another issue has to do with a particular cancer itself. In order for a test to be helpful, the cancer needs to have a long progression through precancerous stages until finally it develops into full-blown cancer.

An example is colon cancer. Most people who develop colon cancer have precancerous polyps several years before they get the cancer. This is why colonoscopies can be effective at preventing the progression to colon cancer.

If a patient has a colonoscopy, the doctor can detect the presence of polyps. More than that, he can remove the polyps through the scope, hopefully stopping the progression to cancer.

One last, related point is that there needs to be some benefit to early detection of cancer. If a new test can detect cancer six months earlier than existing tests, people will live an average of six months longer with the cancer than before, even if nothing else changes.

The question is whether diagnosing the cancer earlier leads to more effective treatment. Can you take it out before it spreads to the lymph glands and thereby completely avoid the need for chemotherapy?

If treatment and response rates are the same regardless of the stage at which you diagnose a cancer, then screening doesn’t really make sense.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force is a volunteer panel of experts that have reviewed the literature on a variety of tests. Based on the studies that have been conducted regarding the available tests, they make recommendations about the various tests and how often to use them.

This panel tends to be more conservative in their recommendations than many cancer societies. For instance, they recommend every other year for the use of mammograms for women between the ages of 50 and 75, as compared to the yearly screening recommended by other groups.

With each recommendation they give a grade of how good the studies are which support that specific recommendation, along with links for those studies. Their recommendations are well researched. This is helpful for low-risk people trying to decide what testing to do. If someone has a high risk because of family history or exposures, their recommendations are less helpful.

Cancer Challenges

People often discuss cancer as though it was a single entity. As before mentioned, cancer is not just one thing. Skin cancer behaves differently from lymphoma, which in turn behaves differently from sarcomas. The chance that there will ever be a single treatment for all cancer—the “Cure for Cancer” which people talk about, is unlikely.

An even bigger challenge when dealing with cancer cells is that they are very similar to our normal cells. Basically, we are trying to poison the cancer just a little more than the rest of our normal tissues. There are a number of different treatments that are currently available. In Part 2, we will address some of the different options available today and some others that may become available in the future.

Final Thoughts

There are a few things that come to mind when contemplating the subject of cancer.

We do not need to live in fear or make choices out of fear. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness –Isaiah 41:10.

I don’t think that we should fatalistically allow anything to happen that might, simply because it is “God’s will.” We need to make wise choices, then having done so, we should not live in a state of anxiety.

Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Matthew 6:31-34.

Finally, if we can, through wise decisions, prevent a certain cancer from forming or spreading, that seems like a reasonable goal. None of us will live forever in this body, but if we can die of something other than cancer, that seems like a good goal too. May God give us wisdom to care for the body which He has given us.

“¿Por qué aún no tenemos una cura para el cáncer?” me preguntó mi paciente.

Me encogí de hombros. “Hay muchos tipos diferentes de cáncer”, dije. “Para algunos hay curas, mientras que para otros todavía estamos aprendiendo la mejor forma de tratarlos.”

“Creo”, dijo mi paciente con la confianza de quien comparte una teoría supuestamente ultrasecreta. “Creo que en realidad sí existe una cura para el cáncer, pero las farmacéuticas no quieren que la sepamos.”

Negué con la cabeza. “Creo que estamos haciendo lo mejor que podemos”, le dije. “Hemos avanzado mucho en cuanto al tratamiento del cáncer, pero todavía nos queda mucho camino por recorrer.”

El cáncer es una enfermedad temible. Un hombre cristiano me dijo que no le tenía miedo a morir, pero que si pudiera elegir, escogería casi cualquier otra manera de irse antes que morir de cáncer.

Aún más, es algo que parece misterioso. Parece que más personas lo obtienen, y sin embargo nadie sabe realmente por qué.

En este artículo, quisiera tomarme un tiempo para explorar qué es el cáncer y para comentar las pruebas de detección del cáncer. En la segunda parte (en el próximo número), si Dios quiere, discutiré algunos de los tratamientos disponibles para los distintos cánceres.

Mencionaré aquí que soy médico de familia. He cuidado a muchos pacientes con cáncer, pero ciertamente no soy oncólogo, ni sé todo sobre el cáncer. Lo que entiendo, estoy dispuesto a compartirlo.

¿Qué es el cáncer?

Como con muchas cosas, podemos rastrear los orígenes del cáncer hasta la caída del hombre en el Jardín del Edén. Sabemos que Dios creó a los seres humanos perfectos. Tal como fueron creados originalmente, no sólo no tendrían cáncer, sino que tampoco lo habrían desarrollado.

Para entender qué es el cáncer, necesitamos comprender cómo se comportan los tejidos y las células normales.

Las células normales viven durante un periodo de tiempo y luego mueren. Este proceso se llama apoptosis. Asegura que haya una renovación constante de células. También evita que un tipo de célula se “descontrole” y comience a crecer en un lugar donde no corresponde.

Cada vez que nuestras células se dividen, copian su ADN en las células hijas. Por lo general esto ocurre sin errores, pero ocasionalmente hay un error en el proceso de copia. Llamamos a estos errores mutaciones.

Las células cancerosas son células que han perdido los frenos normales de su comportamiento. Debido a mutaciones en su ADN, ya no tienen una vida limitada, ni respetan los límites de dónde pertenecen dentro del cuerpo. En cambio, comienzan a invadir los tejidos circundantes, atrayendo en el proceso suministro sanguíneo y nutrientes adicionales.

Las células cancerosas pueden crecer localmente, o pueden diseminarse a través del sistema linfático o circulatorio a partes distantes del cuerpo. Cuando las células cancerosas aparecen en otros lugares distintos al de su origen, lo llamamos metástasis.

El tipo de cáncer se determina por el tipo de célula que se está multiplicando sin control. Los médicos no suelen hablar de “cáncer de piel”, aunque existen cánceres que se originan en células de la piel. En cambio, clasifican estos cánceres en carcinoma de células basales, carcinoma de células escamosas y melanoma, cada uno refiriéndose a un tipo distinto de célula cutánea. Cada uno de estos cánceres de piel se comporta de forma diferente. El carcinoma de células basales y el carcinoma de células escamosas crecen en un área local y rara vez se diseminan, mientras que el melanoma tiende mucho a extenderse a otras partes del cuerpo.

Además, la forma en que un cáncer responde al tratamiento se basará en el tipo de célula del que provenga, no simplemente en el órgano donde se origine.

Causas de las mutaciones…

No sabemos con qué frecuencia ocurría el cáncer en los días previos al diluvio. Yo especularía que era bastante raro.

Sabemos que antes del diluvio, las personas vivían hasta edades muy avanzadas—frecuentemente hasta sus 900 años. Las mutaciones debieron de ser raras. Su ADN estaba más cercano al espécimen genético original de la humanidad (y, por tanto, a la perfección) que el nuestro en el siglo XXI (d. C.). Por lo tanto, la probabilidad de que los genes mutaran y surgieran genes anormales era mucho menor que ahora.

…Factores ambientales

Además de eso, algo debió ocurrir alrededor del tiempo del diluvio que incrementó la tasa de mutaciones. Tal vez hubo un aumento en los niveles de radiación. Quizá hubo cambios genéticos que gradualmente provocaron la aparición del cáncer.

El cáncer no se menciona en la Biblia, aunque es posible que la “piel” (o llaga) de Ezequías pudiera haber sido algún tipo de crecimiento canceroso. También es posible que algunas de las enfermedades que afectaron a los filisteos cuando el arca del pacto estuvo en su tierra fueran tumores cancerosos.

Las personas empezaron a morir a edades más jóvenes después del diluvio y, poco después de la época de Abraham, rara vez vivían mucho más allá de su centésimo año.

Hoy sabemos que las cosas que dañan el mecanismo de copia de la célula y su ADN aumentan el riesgo de cáncer. La más conocida de estas es la radiación.

Después de que se lanzaron las bombas atómicas sobre Hiroshima y Nagasaki, se observó que los supervivientes presentaban incrementos significativos en ciertos tipos de cáncer. La leucemia (cáncer de la sangre) fue el tipo de cáncer más común, seguida por cáncer de estómago, pulmón, hígado y mama.

La radiación no es algo con lo que la mayoría de la gente trate de forma habitual. Sin embargo, si trabajas en un departamento de rayos X o si necesitaste radiación para tratar algún tipo de cáncer, es posible que hayas estado expuesto a niveles de radiación mucho más altos que el público en general.

Hay muchas otras cosas asociadas con aumentos en el cáncer. La exposición a la luz ultravioleta aumenta el riesgo de cáncer de piel y es una de las principales razones por las que los médicos recomiendan protector solar y ropa protectora al disfrutar del sol, para limitar la exposición a los rayos ultravioleta.

Finalmente, existen numerosos químicos presentes en distintos tipos de trabajo que pueden aumentar el riesgo de cáncer.

…Alimentos insalubres

Los alimentos ricos en nitritos aumentan el riesgo de cáncer intestinal. Los nitritos suelen estar presentes en carnes ahumadas y curadas. Por tanto, para estar sanos, las personas deberían limitar su consumo de estos alimentos a ninguno o, como mínimo, a un porcentaje muy limitado de la dieta total.

…Ciertas enfermedades previas

Otra cosa a mencionar es que ciertos tipos de infecciones pueden aumentar el riesgo de cáncer. El virus de Epstein-Barr, que causa la mononucleosis infecciosa, se ha asociado con ciertos tipos de linfoma. La hepatitis B y C aumentan el riesgo de carcinoma hepatocelular (cáncer de hígado). Y las infecciones por Helicobacter pylori en el estómago se asocian con cánceres gástricos.

Es importante recordar que el hecho de que alguien haya tenido uno de estos virus no significa necesariamente que vaya a contraer cáncer por esa infección. Más bien, simplemente aumenta el riesgo de que la persona infectada desarrolle cáncer en algún momento en el futuro.

…Hábitos poco saludables

Una última cosa a mencionar es que ciertas toxinas aumentan drásticamente el riesgo de cáncer. Una obvia es el consumo de tabaco, que incrementa fuertemente el riesgo de cáncer de pulmón, cáncer de garganta e incluso cáncer de vejiga. El alcohol es otro factor de riesgo. El alcohol aumenta el riesgo de cánceres de boca y garganta, cánceres gastrointestinales y cáncer de hígado. Realmente no existe una cantidad segura de exposición a ninguno de estos agentes tóxicos, pero sin duda cuanto mayor sea el nivel de exposición, peor será.

Detección del cáncer

Hay muchas pruebas disponibles que afirman poder detectar una variedad de cánceres. La mayoría de ellas son al menos un poco efectivas para identificar los cánceres en una etapa temprana. Sin embargo, hay algunos problemas con algunas de ellas que indican que cierta prueba es ineficaz para ayudar realmente en el proceso de detección.

Un buen punto de partida es pensar simplemente en cómo sería una prueba de detección perfecta. Esto nos ayudará a ver dónde las pruebas podrían ser beneficiosas o no.

Una prueba de detección perfecta tendrá varias características. Primero, no dará resultados falsos positivos ni falsos negativos. En otras palabras, todos los que den positivo con la prueba tendrán cáncer y los que den negativo no tendrán cáncer. A continuación, la prueba identificará el cáncer en un punto lo suficientemente temprano en su desarrollo como para que sea fácil de tratar. La prueba será barata y mínimamente invasiva, y requerirá una exposición mínima a la radiación.

Desafortunadamente, ninguna prueba que usemos actualmente para la detección cumple totalmente estos criterios.

Por un lado, muchas pruebas producen tanto resultados falsos positivos como falsos negativos. Ambos son problemas. La cuestión con una prueba falsa negativa es obvia: lleva a que alguien piense que no tiene cáncer cuando en realidad sí lo tiene. Un resultado falso positivo, por otro lado, conduce a mayores niveles de ansiedad junto con el costo y los peligros de las pruebas posteriores necesarias para informar al paciente de que en realidad no tiene cáncer.

Un ejemplo de una mala prueba, en este sentido, es el CEA-125. El CEA-125 es una sustancia química que producen algunos tipos de cáncer. Los oncólogos usan este nivel para seguir la respuesta de un paciente a la quimioterapia.

Tendría sentido usar esto como prueba de detección para esos cánceres, pero simplemente no funciona. Muchas personas tienen niveles elevados de CEA, aunque no tengan cáncer y, por otro lado, muchos cánceres gastrointestinales no producen esta sustancia en absoluto. Hacer pruebas de CEA-125 a muchas personas conducirá a más exploraciones y biopsias, pero es dudoso que tenga un impacto significativo en las tasas de mortalidad por cáncer.

Otro problema tiene que ver con el propio cáncer. Para que una prueba sea útil, el cáncer necesita tener una progresión larga a través de etapas precancerosas hasta que finalmente se desarrolla en cáncer pleno.

Un ejemplo es el cáncer de colon. La mayoría de las personas que desarrollan cáncer de colon tienen pólipos precancerosos varios años antes de que aparezca el cáncer. Por eso las colonoscopias pueden ser eficaces para prevenir la progresión hacia el cáncer de colon.

Si un paciente se somete a una colonoscopia, el médico puede detectar la presencia de pólipos. Además, puede extirpar los pólipos a través del endoscopio, con suerte deteniendo la progresión hacia el cáncer.

Un último punto relacionado es que debe existir algún beneficio en la detección temprana del cáncer. Si una nueva prueba puede detectar un cáncer seis meses antes que las pruebas existentes, las personas vivirán en promedio seis meses más con el cáncer que antes, incluso si nada más cambia.

La pregunta es si diagnosticar el cáncer antes conduce a tratamientos más efectivos. ¿Se puede extirpar antes de que se disemine a los ganglios linfáticos y así evitar por completo la necesidad de quimioterapia?

Si las tasas de tratamiento y respuesta son las mismas independientemente de la etapa en que se diagnostique un cáncer, entonces la detección no tiene mucho sentido.

El United States Preventive Services Task Force es un panel voluntario de expertos que ha revisado la bibliografía sobre una variedad de pruebas. Basándose en los estudios realizados respecto a las pruebas disponibles, hacen recomendaciones sobre las distintas pruebas y con qué frecuencia usarlas.

Este panel tiende a ser más conservador en sus recomendaciones que muchas sociedades contra el cáncer. Por ejemplo, recomiendan cada dos años el uso de mamografías para mujeres entre 50 y 75 años, en comparación con el cribado anual recomendado por otros grupos.

Con cada recomendación dan una calificación sobre la calidad de los estudios que respaldan esa recomendación específica, junto con enlaces a esos estudios. Sus recomendaciones están bien investigadas. Esto es útil para personas de bajo riesgo que intentan decidir qué pruebas realizar. Si alguien tiene un alto riesgo por antecedentes familiares o exposiciones, sus recomendaciones son menos útiles.

Desafíos del cáncer

La gente a menudo habla del cáncer como si fuera una única entidad. Como se mencionó antes, el cáncer no es solo una cosa. El cáncer de piel se comporta de forma diferente al linfoma, que a su vez se comporta de forma diferente a los sarcomas. La posibilidad de que alguna vez exista un tratamiento único para todos los cánceres—la “cura para el cáncer” de la que habla la gente—es poco probable.

Un desafío aún mayor al tratar con células cancerosas es que son muy similares a nuestras células normales. Básicamente, intentamos envenenar al cáncer un poco más que al resto de nuestros tejidos normales. Hay una serie de tratamientos diferentes disponibles en la actualidad. En la Parte 2 abordaremos algunas de las opciones disponibles hoy y otras que pueden llegar a estar disponibles en el futuro.

Reflexiones finales

Hay algunas cosas que vienen a la mente al contemplar el tema del cáncer.

No necesitamos vivir con temor ni tomar decisiones movidos por el miedo. No temas, porque yo estoy contigo; no desmayes, porque yo soy tu Dios. Te fortaleceré, sí, te ayudaré, sí, te sustentaré con la diestra de mi justicia —Isaías 41:10.

No creo que debamos permitir fatalistamente que ocurra cualquier cosa que pueda suceder, simplemente porque sea “la voluntad de Dios”. Necesitamos tomar decisiones sabias y, una vez hecho esto, no vivir en un estado de ansiedad.

No os afanéis, pues, por el día de mañana; porque el día de mañana traerá su afán. Basta a cada día su propio mal. —Mateo 6:31-34.

Finalmente, si podemos, mediante decisiones sabias, prevenir que cierto cáncer se forme o se disemine, eso parece un objetivo razonable. Ninguno de nosotros vivirá para siempre en este cuerpo, pero si podemos morir de algo distinto al cáncer, eso también parece un buen objetivo. Que Dios nos dé sabiduría para cuidar el cuerpo que nos ha dado.

“Why don’t we have a cure for cancer yet?” My patient asked me.

I shrugged. “There are lots of different kinds of cancer,” I said. “For some, there are cures, while for others we are still learning how best to treat them.”

“I think,” my patient said with the confidence that he was supposedly sharing a top-secret theory. “I think there actually is a cure for cancer, but the drug companies just don’t want us to know about it.”

I shook my head. “I think we are doing the best we can,” I told him. “We’ve come a long way when it comes to treatment of cancer, but we still have a long way to go.”

Cancer is a scary illness. One Christian man told me that he wasn’t afraid of dying, but if he had a choice, he would choose almost any other way to go than to die of cancer.

More than that, it is something that seems mysterious. More people seem to be getting it, yet no one really knows why.

In this article, I would like to take some time to explore what cancer is, and to discuss cancer screening tests. In the second part (in the next issue) Lord willing, I will discuss some of the treatments available for cancers.

I will mention here that I am a family doctor. I have cared for many patients with cancer, but I am certainly not an oncologist, nor do I know everything about cancer. What I understand, I am willing to share.

What is Cancer?

As with many things, we can trace the beginnings of cancer back to the fall of man in the Garden of Eden. We know that God created humans perfectly. As originally created, not only did they not have cancer, but they also would not have gotten it either.

In order to understand what cancer is, we need to understand how normal tissue and cells behave.

Normal cells live for a period of time and then die. This process is called apoptosis. It makes certain that there is a constant turnover of cells. It also prevents one type of cell from getting “out of line” and beginning to grow in a place where it doesn’t belong.

Every time our cells divide, they copy their DNA into the daughter cells. Usually this happens without error, but occasionally there is an error in the copy process. We call these errors mutations.

Cancer cells are cells that have lost the normal brakes on their behavior. Because of mutations in their DNA, they no longer have a limited life span, nor do they observe the limits of where they belong within the body. Instead, they begin to encroach on surrounding tissues, pulling in additional blood supply and nutrients in the process.

Cancer cells can enlarge locally, or they can spread through the lymphatic system or circulatory system to distant parts of the body. When cancer cells end up in other locations than where they originated, we call it metastases.

The type of cancer is determined by the type of cell that is multiplying out of control. Doctors don’t generally talk about “skin cancer,” even though there are cancers that originate in skin cells. Instead, they classify these cancers into basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma—each one referring to a different kind of skin cell. Each one of these skin cancers acts differently. Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma get bigger in a local area and seldom spread elsewhere, while melanoma is very prone to spreading to other parts of the body.

Additionally, how a cancer responds to treatment is going to be based on the type of cell that it comes from, not simply the organ where it originates.

Causes of Mutations…

We do not know how common cancer was in the days before the flood. I would speculate that it was fairly rare.

We know that before the flood, men lived to be very old—often into their 900s. Mutations must have been rare. Their DNA was closer to the original genetic specimen of mankind (and thus, to perfection) than ours is in the 21st century (AD) Therefore, the chance of genes mutating and abnormal genes popping up was much less than it is now.

…Environmental Factors

Beyond that, something must have happened around the time of the flood that increased the rate of mutations. Perhaps there was an increase in radiation levels. Maybe there were genetic changes that gradually caused cancer to show up.

Cancer is not mentioned in the Bible, although it is possible that Hezekiah’s “boil” could have been some kind of cancerous growth. It is also possible that some of the diseases that affected the Philistines when the ark of the covenant was in their land were cancerous tumors.

People began dying at younger ages after the flood and by soon after the time of Abraham, they were seldom living much past their one hundredth year.

Today, we know that things which damage a cell’s copying mechanism and its DNA increase the risk of cancer. The most well-known of these is radiation.

After the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, survivors were noted to have significant increases in certain kinds of cancer. Leukemia (cancer of the blood) was the most common type of cancer, followed by cancer of stomach, lung, liver, and breast.

Radiation isn’t something that most people deal with on a regular basis. However, if you work in an x-ray department or if you needed to have radiation to treat some type of cancer, it is possible that you have been exposed to much higher levels of radiation than the general public.

There are plenty of other things that are associated with increases in cancers. Exposure to ultraviolet light increases the risk of skin cancer and is a big reason why doctors recommend sunscreen and protective clothing while enjoying the sunshine to limit ultraviolet exposure.

Finally, there are plenty of chemicals that are present in different types of work that can increase the risk of cancer.

…Unhealthy Foods

Foods that are high in nitrites increase the risk of intestinal cancers. Nitrites are typically present in smoked and cured meats. So, to be healthy, people should limit their intake of these foods to none or at the very least, a very limited percentage of the overall diet.

…Certain Prior Diseases

Another thing to mention is that certain types of infections can increase the risk of cancer. Epstein Barr virus, which causes infectious mononucleosis, has been associated with certain kinds of lymphoma. Hepatitis B and C increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). And Helicobacter pylori infections in the stomach are associated with stomach cancers.

It is important to remember that just because someone has had one of these viruses it will not necessarily cause them to get cancer from that infection. Rather, it simply increases the risk that the person infected will get cancer at some point in the future.

…Unhealthy Habits

One last thing to mention is that certain toxins dramatically increase the risk of cancer. An obvious one is tobacco use, which strongly increases the risk of lung cancer, throat cancer, and even bladder cancer. Alcohol is another risk factor. Alcohol increases the risk of mouth and throat cancers, gastrointestinal cancers, and liver cancer. There really isn’t a safe amount of exposure to either of these toxic agents, but certainly the higher the level of exposure, the worse it is.

Screening for Cancer

There are many tests available that claim to be able to screen for a variety of cancers. Most of them are at least a little effective at identifying cancers at an early stage. However, there are a few problems with some of them which indicate that a certain test is ineffective at truly helping with the screening process.

A good place to start is to simply think about what a perfect screening test would look like. This will help us to see where tests might be beneficial or not.

A perfect screening test is going to have a number of features. First, it will have no false positive or false negative results. In other words, everyone who tests positive with the test will have cancer and those who test negative will not have cancer. Next, the test will identify the cancer at a point early enough in its development that it is easy to treat. The test will be cheap and minimally invasive, and it will require minimal exposure to radiation.

Unfortunately, no test that we currently do for screening totally meets these criteria.

For one thing, many tests produce both false positive and negative tests. These are both problems. The issue with a false negative test is obvious—it leads to someone thinking they don’t have cancer when they really do. A false positive test on the other hand leads to higher anxiety levels along with the cost and dangers from whatever ongoing testing is necessary to let a patient know that they don’t really have cancer.

An example of a bad test, in this respect, is the CEA-125. CEA-125 is a chemical that is made by some types of cancer. Oncologists use this level to track a patient’s response to chemotherapy.

It would make sense that you could use this as a screening test for these cancers, but it simply doesn’t work. Many people have elevated CEA levels, even though they don’t have cancer and on the other side, plenty of GI (gastrointestinal) cancers don’t make this chemical at all. Testing lots of people with CEA-125 testing will lead to more scans and biopsies, but it is doubtful if it would have a significant impact on death rates from cancer.

Another issue has to do with a particular cancer itself. In order for a test to be helpful, the cancer needs to have a long progression through precancerous stages until finally it develops into full-blown cancer.

An example is colon cancer. Most people who develop colon cancer have precancerous polyps several years before they get the cancer. This is why colonoscopies can be effective at preventing the progression to colon cancer.

If a patient has a colonoscopy, the doctor can detect the presence of polyps. More than that, he can remove the polyps through the scope, hopefully stopping the progression to cancer.

One last, related point is that there needs to be some benefit to early detection of cancer. If a new test can detect cancer six months earlier than existing tests, people will live an average of six months longer with the cancer than before, even if nothing else changes.

The question is whether diagnosing the cancer earlier leads to more effective treatment. Can you take it out before it spreads to the lymph glands and thereby completely avoid the need for chemotherapy?

If treatment and response rates are the same regardless of the stage at which you diagnose a cancer, then screening doesn’t really make sense.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force is a volunteer panel of experts that have reviewed the literature on a variety of tests. Based on the studies that have been conducted regarding the available tests, they make recommendations about the various tests and how often to use them.

This panel tends to be more conservative in their recommendations than many cancer societies. For instance, they recommend every other year for the use of mammograms for women between the ages of 50 and 75, as compared to the yearly screening recommended by other groups.

With each recommendation they give a grade of how good the studies are which support that specific recommendation, along with links for those studies. Their recommendations are well researched. This is helpful for low-risk people trying to decide what testing to do. If someone has a high risk because of family history or exposures, their recommendations are less helpful.

Cancer Challenges

People often discuss cancer as though it was a single entity. As before mentioned, cancer is not just one thing. Skin cancer behaves differently from lymphoma, which in turn behaves differently from sarcomas. The chance that there will ever be a single treatment for all cancer—the “Cure for Cancer” which people talk about, is unlikely.

An even bigger challenge when dealing with cancer cells is that they are very similar to our normal cells. Basically, we are trying to poison the cancer just a little more than the rest of our normal tissues. There are a number of different treatments that are currently available. In Part 2, we will address some of the different options available today and some others that may become available in the future.

Final Thoughts

There are a few things that come to mind when contemplating the subject of cancer.

We do not need to live in fear or make choices out of fear. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness –Isaiah 41:10.

I don’t think that we should fatalistically allow anything to happen that might, simply because it is “God’s will.” We need to make wise choices, then having done so, we should not live in a state of anxiety.

Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Matthew 6:31-34.

Finally, if we can, through wise decisions, prevent a certain cancer from forming or spreading, that seems like a reasonable goal. None of us will live forever in this body, but if we can die of something other than cancer, that seems like a good goal too. May God give us wisdom to care for the body which He has given us.
